newsitem.title: UK: IBCA ups ASDA long-term rating to A.
newsitem.headline: IBCA ups ASDA long-term rating to A.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Thursday it had raised the long-term rating of ASDA Group Plc to A from A minus.
The short-term rating remains unchanged at A1, IBCA said.

"Having recovered from the trading and financial difficulties it experienced in the early 1990s, the success of the initial three year recovery plan and the subsequent three year "Breakout" programme of growth have contributed to Asda's outperformance of the UK food retail market during the last two years," IBCA said in a statement.

It said that double digit like-for-like sales growth and improved operating margins highlighted the progress made by ASDA in restoring its reputation as the lowest cost food retailer amongst the UK majors, and in enhancing productivity within the core store chain.

"The purchase of the outstanding interests in the Burwood House property joint venture from British Aerospace, and of the outstanding stake in the George Davies partnership, raised net debt at financial-year-end 1996 but ASDA retains a sound financial structure and strong financial coverages," IBCA said.
It said further store openings would be financed from operating cash flow as ASDA sought to expand its "Market Hall Superstore" format and develop the "George" range of own brand clothing.
"Although the pace of progress is likely to slow with the recovery phase now complete, earnings growth should continue despite a highly competitive market," IBCA said.
"With little change expected in net debt, coverages should rise further in line with growth in earnings."
